title: THE BUSH THAT WOULD NOT BURN UP

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "There the angel of the Lord appeared to him in flames of fire from within a bush. Moses saw that though the bush was on fire it did not burn up. So Moses thought, "I will go over and see this strange sight—why the bush does not burn up."" - Exodus 3:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A desert bush on fire would not be strange. Dry thorn scrub burns fast and is gone in minutes. What stopped Moses was that the fire kept burning and the bush was still there.

Fire in Scripture often speaks of God's holiness and His purifying presence. And here is the wonder: the holy God draws near to something ordinary and fragile — a common desert bush — and does not destroy it.

That is the heart of grace. God's holiness could rightly consume us. Instead, in Christ, He comes near to sinners and we are not consumed. As Lamentations puts it, it is because of the Lord's great love that we are not consumed (Lam 3:22).

Notice too that Moses had to turn aside to look. God did not force the encounter. He put something before an old shepherd and waited to see whether he would stop and pay attention.

God is speaking through many things in your day. The question is whether you will slow down enough to turn aside and look.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What might God be showing me that I have been too busy to notice?
2. Do I think of God's holiness as something that threatens me, or as something that has spared me in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, thank You that You draw near without destroying me. Slow me down today so I do not miss what You are showing me. Amen.
